nodes.summary: It is not the case that for every natural number $k \ge 2$ the ratio $\mathrm{ex}(n; \{C_{2k-1}, C_{2k}\}) / (n/2)^{1 + 1/k}$ tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$. Here $\mathrm{ex}(n; \{C_{2k-1}, C_{2k}\})$ is the extremal number: the supremum of the numbers of edges of simple graphs on $n$ vertices that contain no copy of the cycle graph $C_{2k-1}$ and no copy of the cycle graph $C_{2k}$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 574 is false

nodes.title: Erdős Problem 574

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, $\mathrm{ex}(n; \{C_{2k-1}, C_{2k}\})$ is the supremum of the numbers of edges of the simple graphs on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that contain no copy of the cycle graph $C_{2k-1}$ and no copy of the cycle graph $C_{2k}$, where the supremum of the empty set is $0$. Here $2k-1$ is computed in the natural numbers, so it is $0$ when $k = 0$.
nodes.title: Extremal number for cycles of lengths $2k-1$ and $2k$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, a simple graph $G$ is free of the cycle lengths $2k-1$ and $2k$ when it contains no copy of the cycle graph $C_{2k-1}$ and no copy of the cycle graph $C_{2k}$, where a copy is an injective graph homomorphism, that is, a subgraph that need not be induced.
nodes.title: Graphs without cycles of lengths $2k-1$ and $2k$
